summary: Second-pass, read-only review of 3f8995478..HEAD (store gate 9cb7f2204, remote hardening 8e96a2f64, docs 403d0ba44). I had no git/exec tools, so I read the changed files plus the pinned Basalt/UCAN/replay code they call; nothing was built or run, and the worker's rail counts are unverified by me (I only confirmed 16 tests exist in attenuated_admission_tests.rs and counted 22 refusal-case names). WT=/home/brittonr/.cargo-target/agents-20261030/attenuation/worktree. DISPOSITIONS: F2 PARTLY fixed (job_id/attempt shape/class/sorted output names are now caveat-visible; payload, inputs, limits are not and only the status record says so). F5 FIXED (digest = domain v2 + endpoint id + serde_json of the whole ConcreteBuildRequest; 14 field mutations tested; ticket id deliberately unbound and disclosed). F6 FIXED (check_loadable at start; 12 failure modes tested at helper level). F7 PARTLY fixed (loopback, frame-level and fixture paths refuse before bearer check, redemption and state save; default executor, hello capability and older receivers unchanged but documented). F8-lite PARTLY fixed (restricted `store info` gated before open_store with an ordering test; no production producer and unredacted references remain, documented). F9 FIXED but REGRESSED (reason codes logged, audit line moved after redemption; the sink is stderr, which the ssh-stdio client relays to the sender). F11 FIXED for the stated defect (before-snapshots incl. ledger bytes, 22 cases) with residual gaps and one new vacuous assertion. F12-lite PARTLY fixed (zero-caveat UCAN labelled ucan-unrestricted; nested goals and missing producers documented, not changed). NEW PROBLEMS: R2-1 (medium) the variable-length output tail makes reject/wildcard caveats shape-dependent and evadable by padding, and a complete job-id reject is inexpressible within the 8-caveat/8-alternative bounds; R2-2 denial reason codes reach the sender over stdio-once/ssh-stdio while docs and comments say 'never sent' (I5 'no reason' violated on the primary remote binding); R2-3 the start check couples legacy bearer service to snapshot validity; plus test, digest-contract and doc nits (R2-4..R2-8). CLEAN: no collision or forgery in the target encoding (positional, injective, vocabulary identical to the core), no log injection, no panic sites in new production code, no state change before any refusal (production, loopback, frame-level, fixture), check_loadable is read-only and fail-closed, store info is gated before open_store. Recommendation: merge as not-accepted groundwork; fix R2-1 and the R2-2 log/claim before any task is ticked or an enforcing mode is built.

findings.title: Variable-length output-name tail makes reject (denylist) and wildcard caveats shape-dependent: a reject on a job id or class is evaded by padding the declared output set, and a complete reject cannot be written within the chain bounds
findings.evidence: job_target appends every declared output name as its own segment: `names.sort_unstable(); ... segments.extend(names);` (attenuated_admission.rs:131-139). The filter matches whole values only, `if values.next().is_some() { return None; }` (caveat.rs:113-115), there is no multi-segment wildcard, and a reject passes every non-matching value through: `Filter::Reject(pattern) => if pattern.bindings(value).is_some() { None } else { ... Some(value) }` (caveat.rs:237-244). MAX_ALTERNATIVES=8 and MAX_CHAIN=8 (caveat.rs:22-23) while 9 shapes (1..9 names) are bindable (attenuated_admission.rs:97), and caveats AND-compose, they do not union. Production accepts up to 128 outputs (remote_build.rs:163) and always carries an attempt (remote_build.rs:13283-13284). The tests only use exact-target allow/reject (tests:430-433, 696-740), never a padded set.
findings.scenario: H holds a grant whose parent allows two shapes, e.g. `/job/:r/attempt/:j/class/action/outputs/:o` and `.../outputs/:o/:p`, and sub-delegates to D with an appended `reject /job/secret/attempt/:j/class/action/outputs/:o` meaning 'never job secret'. D submits request_id secret with outputs [a,b]: the target `/job/secret/attempt/J/class/action/outputs/a/b` has 9 segments, the reject pattern has 8, so the reject does not match and the chain admits it. Even an expert cannot write a full job-id reject: it needs 9 reject caveats for 9 shapes and the chain holds 8. Padding looks feasible because derivation outputs come from the holder's own derivation JSON and action outputs from the spec [INFERENCE: I did not read validate_derivation_plan_identity/validate_action_spec bodies]. In the first-pass target `/job/<id>/output/<class>` the shape was fixed and a reject on a job id was complete; this tail is new (it follows my F2 recommendation, so the fix should be reshaped). Allowlist (rewrite) caveats that pin the exact target are unaffected, and in today's advisory mode a bearer holder can drop the presentation anyway, so the impact falls on the intended bearer-less holder-to-delegate attenuation model.
findings.recommendation: Give the filters a fixed-shape target: put the output set in ONE segment (e.g. `outputs/<blake3 of the length-framed sorted names>`) or leave outputs out of the filter-visible target and bind them only via the digest, so a reject on job id/class is complete. At minimum refuse chains with no allowlist rewrite, document that reject caveats are shape-exact, and add a padded-outputs negative fixture. Also note exact pins are capped at 256 bytes (caveat.rs:24,77,136) although targets may reach 512.

findings.title: Denial reason codes are warned to stderr at the default level; in stdio-once/ssh-stdio the client relays remote stderr to the sender, so reason classes reach the sender while docs, status and code comments say 'never sent'
findings.evidence: `tracing::warn!(target: 'mantle::remote::attenuation', reason = reason.code(), 'attenuated grant denied')` (remote_build.rs:13619; non-enforcing refusal :13631-13635). init_tracing starts a stderr subscriber at WARN in the default human format (main.rs:3624-3643; crates/mantle-application-contract/src/output_format.rs logging_decision: human always initialised, `--json` without a log flag suppresses). The client drains the remote child's stderr and embeds it in its errors and transcript: `stderr_tx.send(drain_bounded_pipe(stderr, ...))` (remote_build.rs:9878-9880), `stderr={}` (9938-9941, 10094-10100), `transcript.stderr_summary = ...` (9948-9951). The documented serve invocation has no --json (docs:117-122). Claims: docs:143 'shows the sender only ... never ... reason ... (never sent)'; attenuated_admission.rs:216 'never sent to the sender' and :196-199 'LOCAL diagnostics only'; status follow-up 6 'never sent'; spec scenario 'MUST NOT ... expose any reason to the sender'. Static trace, not executed.
findings.scenario: A holder with a valid bearer probes a receiver over ssh-stdio. Each denial prints `WARN mantle::remote::attenuation: attenuated grant denied reason=...` on the remote stderr, which the client shows. The sender can tell no-operator-authority (receiver has no snapshot), request-unbindable, presentation-malformed and project-scope-mismatch apart from the catch-all verification-denied, and by trying project strings can discover the receiver's endpoint scope (mismatch vs verification-denied). Before this change every denial was one indistinguishable constant. On the fixture executor a ticketless peer presenting a junk grant is told non-enforcing-admission-path before the bearer is even checked, fingerprinting the executor. Information value is low (no job, path, caveat, revocation or time detail; verification-denied is a catch-all), but the claim is false and I5 'no reason' no longer holds on the primary remote binding.
findings.recommendation: Do not emit reason codes on a stream the peer can read: send them to a receiver-local sink (journal/file) or gate them behind an explicit opt-in target, keep default stderr to the constant, and correct the docs, doc comments and status wording. Add a tracing-capture test on the serve path.

findings.title: Start check ties legacy bearer service to snapshot validity, runs late, and gives the operator no reason; docs still say bearer-only requests are 'unchanged'
findings.evidence: `let attenuation_verifier = attenuated_admission::open_operator_authority(input.state_dir)?;` precedes `match local_executor` (remote_build.rs:14285-14286), so for every executor, including the default fixture one, a provisioned snapshot that is expired (`now >= snapshot.expires_unix_s`, authority.rs:185), not yet issued, wrong hash, etc. makes `remote serve` exit with `remote-attenuation-authority-invalid` before it reads a frame (attenuated_admission.rs:292-305). It runs after resolve_remote_service_keys_bounded, remote_serve_executor and ReadinessPublisher::start_service (remote_build.rs:14233-14284). All twelve tested failure modes print the same constant. docs:139 says requests without a presentation use the bearer path 'unchanged'; only docs:147 says the server refuses to start.
findings.scenario: An operator provisions attenuation-authority.json with a 7-day window to try grants. On day 8 every `remote serve` fails, so legacy bearer-only builds stop until the file is refreshed or removed. Diagnosing which of the twelve conditions failed needs guesswork (a code on stderr would itself reach an ssh peer, see R2-2).
findings.recommendation: If fail-closed start is intended, say so next to the 'unchanged' sentence (docs:139); otherwise fail only the presented-grant path (operator-side log) and keep bearer-only serving. Give the operator a local diagnostic (e.g. an offline `check` command) that does not run on the peer channel.

findings.title: Test gaps: frame-level non-enforcing assertion is vacuous and its control weak; refusal cases cannot attribute the refusing check; key negatives, serve wiring and logs are unexercised
findings.evidence: The `admit` closure passes `&mut ticket.clone()` (line 1006), so `assert_eq!(ticket.uses_remaining, fixture_ticket().uses_remaining)` (line 1018) can never fail; the frames stop after auth, so redemption is unreachable even without the refusal; the no-grant control is only `assert_ne!(.., Some(ATTENUATED_GRANT_DENIED))` (line 1015), which any other error satisfies. The 22-case loop asserts only the constant string (610, 369-377), so a mutation refused for an unintended reason still passes; only grant_for_one_job_id... and every_request_field... assert DenialReason::Verification. Not exercised at the receiver: untrusted root issuer, unknown holder key, parent proof absent from the snapshot, tampered token body (Verifier::check_roots/key resolution), unregistered caveat domain/type, duplicate ordinal; serve-path negatives other than unknown caveat (1072-1093); serve_stdio_remote_fixture_once and cmd_remote_serve (start wiring, executor default); any log output; concurrent presentations; ledger full/write failure; the verified-then-redemption-failed abort (remote_build.rs:13573-13581); the rollback-guard seeding.
findings.scenario: A regression that silently accepted a grant from an untrusted root, or one that made a case fail for a fixture bug, would pass this suite; the frame-level 'no redemption' claim is proven only by structure, not by the test.
findings.recommendation: Assert on the real ticket and on the exact next error for the frame-level case; pair each mutation with a positive control or assert DenialReason per case via verify_directly; add the missing negatives, a cmd_remote_serve/fixture-executor start test and a tracing-capture test.

findings.title: The whole-request digest is an implicit serde struct-order contract with no golden vector, no external-signer spec, and an unzeroized request copy
findings.evidence: digest = BLAKE3(domain v2 || frame(endpoint_id) || frame(serde_json::to_vec(request))). The determinism test compares the implementation with itself and a serde round trip only (tests:859-868); there is no pinned digest vector. endpoint_binding (generation, expires_unix_s) is inside the JSON, so binding rotation changes every digest. The encoded Vec (bounded by the 1 MiB frame, remote_build.rs:165) is a plain allocation although the wire frame is zeroized (remote_build.rs:8699); ConcreteBuildRequest itself carries no ticket secret (TicketAuthRequest is separate and not serialised).
findings.scenario: A later refactor reorders ConcreteBuildRequest fields or adds a serialized field: every outstanding presentation and any non-Rust signer silently stops matching (fail-closed, no test fails). Rotating the endpoint binding invalidates all outstanding presentations. A coordinator retry (new attempt_id/fence_generation) needs a new holder signature and a new ledger slot.
findings.recommendation: Pin a golden vector (request JSON bytes + digest) in a test, document the canonical encoding for external signers, and zeroize the encoded buffer or hash through a streaming serializer.

findings.title: F2 residual is stated only in the status record: operator docs still say the caveats 'restrict one job' although payload, inputs, limits and registration of the label are not caveat-visible
findings.evidence: The filter-visible identity is request_id, optional job_id, kind and output names only (attenuated_admission.rs:122-146). docs:139 says the preserved caveats 'restrict one job'; docs:159 says no sender-supplied 'job' is trusted. The status record says a grant 'still admits any payload body, input set or resource request that keeps the label' (status line 9); the docs do not. The label (request_id, job_id) is sender-chosen and not tied to a coordinator-registered job. A 64-hex payload-digest segment would fit the filter vocabulary but is not used.
findings.scenario: An operator reads the docs and believes a one-job grant limits what is built; the holder signs any payload under the granted label and repeats it for as many attempts as ticket uses and ledger slots allow.
findings.recommendation: State the residual in docs/remote-credentials.md; consider a payload-digest segment (trading names out of the target if the 16-segment budget is tight, which also helps R2-1).

findings.title: Remaining overclaiming or stale sentences in docs, code comments and the core crate
findings.evidence: (a) docs:143, attenuated_admission.rs:196-199,216, status item 6: 'never sent' / 'shows the sender only' (see R2-2). (b) docs:139 'use the bearer path above, unchanged' vs start refusal (R2-3). (c) docs:139 'restrict one job' without the F2 residual (R2-6). (d) docs:147 'the rollback guard is per process and remote serve is stdio-once, so restoring an older snapshot is accepted' is understated after check_loadable seeds the guard on the same verifier that serves the single request (authority.rs:195-198,218): a lower revision or same-revision-different-bytes file between start and the first presentation is now refused; the sentence holds only across starts. (e) docs:159 'No sender-supplied ... job ... is trusted' is ambiguous because the job label is sender-chosen and only matched against caveats. (f) caveat.rs:406-410 still documents `/job/<request-id>/output/<validated-class>` for admit_remote_job, which no shell uses (only core tests), while the shell target is `/job/<id>[/attempt/<id>]/class/<kind>/outputs/...`.
findings.scenario: Operators and later reviewers rely on the stated guarantees; (a) and (b) are the ones that mislead about denial uniformity and legacy availability.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the listed sentences; keep the advisory banner and the ticket-id-unbound disclosure as they are.

findings.title: Operational consequences of the new target and digest (all fail-closed)
findings.evidence: The production receiver rejects requests without production_attempt (remote_build.rs:13283-13284), so only the attempt-shaped target is reachable in production; docs:141 shows the attempt segments as optional. Only 9 of the 128 allowed outputs (remote_build.rs:163) are bindable (attenuated_admission.rs:97,133); a no-attempt request could carry 11 but is capped at 9 as well. The digest covers attempt_id and fence_generation.
findings.scenario: A grant authored for the plain shape never matches in production; multi-output derivations with more than 9 outputs cannot use a grant; every coordinator retry needs a fresh holder signature, nonce and ledger slot (F3 capacity).
findings.recommendation: Document the attempt-only reality and the 9-output cap next to the target format.

invariants.name: I5 A denied request sends no protocol frame and leaks no job, path, caveat or reason to the sender and redeems no ticket, reads no store path, evaluates no project goal
invariants.evidence: Holds for frames, job, path, caveat, redemption, store reads and goals: commit(...)? at remote_build.rs:13293 precedes the first write at 13296; refusal precedes redemption (13561-13564); the fixture path returns before save_ticket_state (14352); denial logs carry no request id, token, caveat or path. Violated for 'reason' on the stdio-once / ssh-stdio bindings at default logging: reason codes are warned to stderr (remote_build.rs:13619, 13631-13635) and the client relays remote stderr (9878-9880, 9938-9941, 10094-10100). Static trace, not executed. See R2-2.

questions.answer: Target `/job/<request_id>[/attempt/<job_id>]/class/<kind>/outputs/<sorted names>`. Collision/injection: none found. job_target (WT/src/remote_build/attenuated_admission.rs:122-146) rejects the whole request unless every segment passes is_filter_segment (:111-117), which is identical to the core vocabulary (WT/crates/crunch-remote-core/src/caveat.rs:362-367: ASCII alnum plus `+._?=-`, non-empty, not `.`/`..`, so no `/` and no `:`), hence join('/') is injective and split recovers the exact list. Positions are fixed: index 2 is `class` without an attempt and `attempt` with one, so no attempt-shaped target equals a plain one whatever the ids or names are; a request_id, job_id or output literally named attempt/class/outputs only fills its own slot, and the tail after `outputs` is exactly the sorted name set, so distinct (request_id, job_id|none, kind, name set) tuples give distinct targets. `/`, `:`, percent, non-ASCII, empty and dot segments are refused (RequestUnbindable), never escaped. Tests: tests:743-781 (shape, 9 vs 10 names, duplicates, bad ids `r/1`, `:bind`, `..`, non-ASCII, 600-byte id) and tests:696-740 (other job id, no attempt, fewer/more/renamed outputs, other request id: DenialReason::Verification, ledger untouched). Bounds: names <= 9 (const :97 = MAX_SEGMENTS-7, checked at :133 before any use), segments <= 16, total <= 512 bytes (:140-143), duplicates/empty refused, nothing truncated. Two practical limits: exact identity pins are capped at 256 bytes because pattern/template parsing caps at MAX_PATTERN_BYTES=256 (caveat.rs:24,77,136) although targets may reach 512; production allows 128 outputs (remote_build.rs:163) but only 9 are bindable. Design match: design.md:63-67 wants request_id, the validated production_attempt.job_id when an attempt exists, the payload kind and declared output names: all present; payload content is not (R2-6). The production receiver requires an attempt (remote_build.rs:13283-13284), so the plain shape is unreachable in production. What does bite is shape-dependence, not forgery: R2-1.

Digest (attenuated_admission.rs:158-175, domain v2 at :45): BLAKE3(domain || u64be-len||endpoint_id || u64be-len||serde_json::to_vec(request)). Deterministic on the decoded value: fields in declaration order (remote_build.rs:403-430), skip_serializing_if omits only None/empty-default values (so None and Some('') are now distinct, unlike the old `unwrap_or('')`), serde_json escaping and decimal integers are stable. I read every request-reachable nested type: RemoteTransferPolicy (crates/crunch-build/src/distributed/remote_transfer.rs:189-201, Copy ints), RemoteResourceRequirements/Vector/NamedQuantity (remote_resources.rs:68-97), RemoteLocalityScope (:180-184), RemoteFailureDebugPolicy + capture policy (remote_failure_debug.rs:119-150), EndpointBinding(Spec) (crates/crunch-remote-core/src/endpoint.rs:29-45), attempt ids `serde(transparent)` (attempt.rs:33-34,48-49,121-122): no HashMap, float, serde_json::Value or preserve_order dependency (the BTreeMaps in those files are internal, not request fields). Re-serialising the decoded struct means wire whitespace, key order and \u escapes do not matter; unknown wire fields are dropped (no deny_unknown_fields on ConcreteBuildRequest) and are inert. Length framing + domain separate the two inputs; distinct request values give distinct JSON. Sender/receiver skew only arises if the two builds disagree on the struct definition (fail-closed); endpoint_binding generation/expiry are inside the JSON, so binding rotation invalidates presentations. Secrets: ConcreteBuildRequest carries no ticket secret (TicketAuthRequest is separate, not serialised); the encoded Vec (<= ~1 MiB frame bound, remote_build.rs:165) is plain while the wire frame is zeroized (:8699). No golden vector, no external-signer spec: R2-5.

check_loadable (WT/src/nix_gateway/authority.rs:173-175) = load(now) (:177-226): private_read (O_NOFOLLOW, regular file, owner, mode&0o077==0, <=1 MiB; :551-566), JSON parse, version/window/hash/limit checks (:183-194), policy parse, key and proof parsing (no signature verification), then `*observed = (revision, digest)` (:218). It never calls replay_for or the ledger port (open() only runs require_private_dir, crates/crunch-nix-gateway/src/replay.rs:250-259), writes nothing and consumes no slot. Fail-open: none; absent file is the only Ok(None) (attenuated_admission.rs:294-295); every other stat/open/parse/window error is `remote-attenuation-authority-invalid` (:292-305), tested by 12 failure modes plus a valid control and the unprovisioned case (tests:892-960). Beyond reading, it seeds the in-memory rollback guard of the same verifier that later serves the single request, so a lower revision or same revision with different bytes between start and the first presentation is now refused (before, the guard was first set by the request's own load and never fired); docs:147 'restoring an older snapshot is accepted' is therefore true only across starts (R2-7d). Side effects to know: legacy availability coupling and late placement after secret resolution and store preflight (remote_build.rs:14233-14286): R2-3.

Log injection: no. Denial logs carry only `reason = reason.code()`, a closed enum rendered by a const fn to fixed literals (attenuated_admission.rs:217-229), and literal messages (remote_build.rs:13619, 13631-13635, 13576-13580); no request id, ticket id, caveat, path or token is included. The admitted INFO line (13643-13646, off at the default WARN) prints the redacted chain with `%report` where report is serde_json output: only digests and patterns/templates that passed Caveat::from_wire (vocabulary-limited, authority_caveats.rs describe_caveat), JSON-escaped. Wire: nothing reaches the protocol stream (commit(...)? at remote_build.rs:13293 precedes the first write at 13296; the error text goes to stderr via RunError, 14303). But the log sink is the process stderr at default WARN (main.rs:3624-3643) and in stdio-once/ssh-stdio the client drains and displays remote stderr (remote_build.rs:9878-9880, 9938-9941, 9948-9951, 10094-10100), so the reason code reaches the sender: R2-2. `--json` without a log flag would suppress it (output_format.rs logging_decision); the documented invocation (docs:117-122) does not use it.

Yes, uniformly and before any effect. refuse_presentation_on_non_enforcing_path (remote_build.rs:13627-13637) returns Err(ATTENUATED_GRANT_DENIED) whenever auth.attenuated_grant is Some. Call sites: run_loopback_remote_session (:12033, before expect_authorized_ticket :12034 and redeem_after_queue :12046) and take_auth (:12210, before expect_authorized_ticket :12211), which admit_remote_builder_frames_with_auth_facts calls at :10573 before redeem_after_queue at :10591 and which the default fixture executor path uses (serve_stdio_remote_fixture_once, :14341-14352): on refusal `?` returns before save_ticket_state (:14352), so no state change; the CLI text is `remote fixture stdio serve once: remote-attenuated-grant-denied` (:14351), a fixed prefix plus the constant. The production path is the only enforcing path (commit_remote_ticket_admission_for_state :13561-13562; the nonce is consumed only when verification succeeds, and an exhausted/expired/revoked ticket is refused by the bearer check first, remote_credentials.rs apply_ticket_policy). I found no other site that redeems a ticket (redeem_after_queue is called at :10591, :12046, :13698 only). Caveats: on the non-enforcing paths the refusal precedes the bearer check, so a ticketless peer learns the executor is non-enforcing and a warn line is emitted for unauthenticated input (R2-2); the guard exists only in this build (older receivers, hello capability, executor default: docs:145, main.rs:2801).

Captured BEFORE the call: yes. assert_refused_without_effect now takes `before: &Snapshot` as a parameter (tests:369-377) and every call site captures it first (tests:430, 608, 626, 633, 1088; in the 22-case loop at :608 immediately before admit_at at :609, after the mutations so they are part of the baseline). Snapshot = the whole RemoteTicketState parsed from disk (equality over all fields) plus every file name and byte in the replay directory (tests:238-242, 292-305). Meaningful: the positive tests prove the ledger does change on admission (tests:395, 1124), so the comparison can detect nonce use. 22 cases: counted in refusal_cases() (tests:485-512), each on a freshly built Receiver. NOT proven: (a) which check refused: every case asserts only the constant string, there is no per-case positive control, only grant_for_one_job_id... and every_request_field... assert DenialReason::Verification; (b) untrusted root issuer, unknown holder key, parent proof missing from the snapshot, tampered token body, unregistered caveat domain/type, duplicate ordinal; (c) serve-path negatives other than unknown caveat (tests:1072-1093); (d) the frame-level non-enforcing test: `admit` passes `&mut ticket.clone()` (1006) so the final assertion (1018) is vacuous, the frames stop after auth so redemption is unreachable, and the control is only `assert_ne!(.., Some(DENIED))` (1015); serve_stdio_remote_fixture_once and cmd_remote_serve (start wiring, executor default) are not driven; (e) no log capture, so neither R2-2 nor the redacted INFO line is tested; (f) concurrency, ledger full/write failure, the verified-then-redemption-failed abort (remote_build.rs:13573-13581); (g) the rollback-guard seeding; (h) a golden digest vector. I did not run any rails.

Mostly accurate and much more honest: advisory banner (docs:139), ticket id unbound (docs:141), provisioning (:149), ledger limits and rotation (:151), lock (:153), store/project limits (:157), 'implemented, not accepted' in docs:137 and the status record; tasks.md T3.1-T4.5 are still unticked and ADR 0090, design.md and the spec are unchanged (design.md still says 'nested goal rejected'). Still overclaiming or stale: docs:143 'shows the sender only ... never ... reason' and 'never sent', repeated in attenuated_admission.rs:196-199,216 and status item 6 (false over ssh-stdio stderr, R2-2); docs:139 'use the bearer path above, unchanged' while a provisioned but expired/invalid snapshot stops `remote serve` (R2-3; docs:147 says so only in the authority paragraph); docs:139 'restrict one job' without the F2 residual (only status line 9, R2-6); docs:147 rollback sentence understated after check_loadable seeds the guard (Q3); docs:159 'No sender-supplied ... job ... is trusted' is ambiguous because the label is sender-chosen and only matched; crates/crunch-remote-core/src/caveat.rs:406-410 still documents `/job/<request-id>/output/<validated-class>` for admit_remote_job, which no shell uses. See R2-7.

Per-finding disposition. F2 PARTLY FIXED: job_id/attempt shape, class and sorted output names are caveat-visible (attenuated_admission.rs:122-146); tests:696-740 refuse other job id, no attempt, other/more/fewer outputs and other request id with DenialReason::Verification and an untouched ledger. Not fixed: payload body, inputs, limits, resources and registration of the label are not caveat-visible and operator docs do not say so (R2-6); the fix introduced R2-1. F5 FIXED: bind_remote_job hashes domain v2 + endpoint id + the whole serde_json request (attenuated_admission.rs:45,158-175); tests:788-856 mutate contains_raw_frontend_eval, attempt_id, fence_generation, transfer_policy, resource_requirements, locality_scope, failure_debug_policy, failure_replay, endpoint_binding generation and scope, upload_bytes, input_refs, store_prefix and an expected output path (14 mutations, each asserted to change the request, each refused with DenialReason::Verification and an untouched ledger) plus a control that admits; ticket id intentionally unbound and disclosed (docs:141); residual R2-5.
